quest.title: Suspicions Aroused
quest.description: The second round has come to an end, but there are some matters that haven't been resolved...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.num: A Parade of Providence: Act II
chapter.title: Beginnings and Endings

talks.objective: Go play at an Akademiya booth

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It feels like something's been on your mind this entire time.

choices.text: (That white-haired man I saw before the competition started...)

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon! I've finally found you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Finally"? Did something happen?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Don't you feel like there's something off about this year's Akademiya Extravaganza?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: When Candace and I were at a café earlier, we might've caught sight of some mercs on business. Thing is, they were disguised as tourists here to shop.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: But no disguise can mask the stench of blood. Just from their suspicious looks, I bet they do dirty work like kidnapping or assassinations.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: We eavesdropped on them for a while. Their target seems to be someone called Sachin.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sachin? Isn't that the person who Kareena mentioned during the opening ceremony?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He's apparently the sponsor behind the competition prizes and the Diadem of Knowledge. But he hasn't shown himself at all...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Sounds like a rich person, all right... It makes sense now.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: The Eremites have been struggling to make ends meet recently, so a lot of groups have been doing "private" work that involves the rich.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: In their words, one gig sets you up for half a year. Just one job like this nets them enough Mora to take it easy for a while.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: The Extravaganza has brought many tourists to Sumeru City all at once, so it's likely that they took advantage of the bustle to sneak in.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Dehya and I wanted to directly capture them, but they were on guard and made some excuse to slip away.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I would've tied them up if it wouldn't have caused a scene.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Who's legally supposed to take care of this kind of thing? The matra? Or the Corps of Thirty?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... If Cyno were here, he'd definitely get involved. Why don't we head over to the Akademiya and tell a matra?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks a million, you two!

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Not at all. It was coincidence on our part as well.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yeah, don't sweat it. The Eremites' reputation is gonna get even worse if these scumbags succeed.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: But this is Sumeru City. Candace and I don't have as much freedom to act here, so we're leaving this in your hands.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Should you require our aid, come find us at the café.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's noticed that something's bugging you. Is it the Extravaganza? 'Cause Paimon's starting to think that there's more than meets the eye here, too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, but thinking like this isn't doing anything. Let's just go find a matra!

choices.text: (That secret conversation we overheard after the first round ended...)

talks.objective: Head to the Akademiya and find a matra

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Hello both. It's been a while. Do you have any issues to report?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Aarav about the situation with Dehya and Candace.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Someone's planning to kidnap Sachin? Goodness... Though I suppose it's not all that surprising.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: The growing popularity of the Extravaganza has given him quite the reputation boost as its sponsor. He's seen as one of these "super-rich" types.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, since he's got a target on his back now, shouldn't you send some people to protect him?

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: To tell you the truth, we've thought about doing just that. However, Sachin apparently prefers to spend most of his time out doing field work, and hardly ever comes back to Sumeru City. No one has been able to contact him.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Our only lead is something he once said... "Each time the Interdarshan Championship is held, I will be watching from close by to choose a suitable person to inherit my estate."

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Assuming he remains committed to that promise, then he must be right here in the city somewhere. I suspect that the Eremites in question must've heard about that as well, and decided to come here and try their luck.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So they shouldn't know where Sachin is either, right?

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: I would assume not. Anyway, Mahamatra Cyno is still on vacation, so I'll handle this.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Don't you worry. A couple of kidnappers aren't gonna get very far in Sumeru City these days. I have my ways of forcing them out into the open.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: All of that said — if you're interested in Sachin's story, why don't you try tracking him down as well?

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: The sooner we ascertain his whereabouts, the quicker we can act to ensure his safety. I mean, you could task all the matra and the whole Corps of Thirty with someone's protection, but if the client doesn't show themselves, there's nothing we can do to help them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fair point. Guess we should start searching for him too. But where should we start?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do the matra have any information at all on Sachin?

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: None, I'm afraid. He's never committed any crimes or broken academic protocol, so we don't have a very detailed file on him.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: I've heard that Alhaitham has now stepped down from his post as Acting Grand Sage and is back to being the Scribe again. Maybe it's worth checking to see if he knows anything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good idea. Okay, we'll head back to the Extravaganza venue and see if we can find him!

talks.objective: Go to the main venue and find Alhaitham

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... Hey, Nilou, have you seen Alhaitham anywhere?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Alhaitham? Why, what is it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're trying to track down someone, and we need him to pull up some records for us.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Oh, I see... Sorry, I don't know where he went.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: He's always the first to leave after the competition ends, and he never tells anyone where he'll be going...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Yeah, actually, that sounds about right for him.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Lemme think... To be honest, he doesn't seem very interested in the Extravaganza, so he probably doesn't stick around longer than he has to.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: To him, being a commentator is just extra work he was roped into. Do you guys know of any places he'd go after work?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Uhh... There's still one more round to go. Would he really go to a tavern in the middle of the competition?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Here's a thought. Maybe he just went straight home?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon remembers that his house isn't that far from here, so we might as well check it out!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, maybe!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's try knocking...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Knock.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No answer... Maybe no one's home?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Knock.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hellooo...? Alhaitham? Are you in? We need your help with something!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Kaveh! You're home!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Come on in. I'll get the door for you.

talks.objective: Knock on the door and enter Alhaitham's home

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We didn't hear a peep when we first knocked — we thought no one was home!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Well, I can't be too careful. If someone from the Akademiya came here looking for Alhaitham and I opened the door for them without thinking, before long the whole city would know that I'm living here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're pretty conscientious about this, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... what happens if someone comes inside looking for him while you're at home?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It's fine, as long as I stay in my own room. Anyway, why would someone just barge in here looking for him? Most people have better things to do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fair enough. So do you know where he is at the moment?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What do you think? Who knows what he does in his free time. All that matters to me is that he's out of the house!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you have a quarrel or something?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I wouldn't call it that, he's just incapable of saying anything pleasant at all!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I told him how the second round went. I won the lot draw, remember? Because of good karma, of course. My luck's on the rise.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: But him, being him... You wouldn't believe what he said after I was done talking!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: "You're always quick to remind me that you're my upperclassman, and yet you do not problem-solve in the manner becoming of an upperclassman. This begs the question of why we attach prestige to seniority at all." What does he mean, "manner becoming of an upperclassman"? What, am I supposed to earn the title of upperclassman now!?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: And he didn't stop there! He said:

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: "I'd encourage you to reflect on why you've ended up having to rely on luck every round. Frankly, it's incomprehensible to me how you've managed to make it to this age without acknowledging the proverbial elephant in the room of your life."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hahaha... Yeah, that does sound like something Alhaitham would say...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I've had it with him! Every time I talk to him it's the same way! He finds a way to infuriate me, every single time!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Anyway, the disdain is very much mutual between us, so I'll be moving out as soon as possible. I'm actually packing my things right now. He'll have to get used to doing his own cleaning and tidying from now on!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: See those perfectly hung paintings on the walls? They're coming with me, too! Heh, if his life wasn't utterly devoid of artistic sensibility already, it certainly will be after today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you're moving out already? But the competition isn't even over yet. How can you afford it?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Well, obviously I can't just yet. I'm just packing early, to get ahead of the game.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I've got my new place picked out already. The moment I have my hands on the prize money, I'm going to buy it and move my things right in. It'll take me three days tops to move out of here for good.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I now know what I have to do to achieve this goal. No matter what happens in the third round, I will win. I will emerge triumphant! You'll see!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we'll be rootin' for ya. But... are you sure you'll be alright?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hmm? In what way?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Layla said that she thinks you'll get caught up in internal conflict.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Meaning what, exactly? Don't tell me you think I have serious personality flaws, too...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We didn't say that! But think about it. You say you wanna win, but you also turned Faruzan down when she offered to give you her points. Plus, you took it upon yourself to help those Desert Foxes...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Wait, what's so unusual about all that? I gave you my reasons — I would have felt guilty otherwise... Where's the conflict in that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why would you feel guilty?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Well, when you put it like that... Yes, why, indeed? It's a good question. I guess it's just in my nature. Plus, if I just did nothing, then there'd be no escaping the blame if something bad came of it later down the line.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But thinking like that all the time must make your life so exhausting. Not to mention that by helping out, you put yourself at risk... Fainting in the middle of the desert, for example. Was that really worth it?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It's complicated, I... Look, let's maybe leave this conversation for another time. What was it you needed Alhaitham's help with, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'd like him to help us look into Sachin.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Sachin? Huh, he did actually mention a Sachin recently.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I remember he brought a few documents home that day. He was thinking out loud as he looked through them, making some notes and doodling as he went. He even suggested that I should take a look, but I didn't. Gimme a moment, let me go find them...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ah, this is the one. Here, take it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... You sure he'd be okay with this?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: With taking liberties? He's certainly okay with helping himself to my beer whenever he pleases.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: And anyway, he did ask me if I wanted to read his notes. I didn't see the point at the time, so he just left them on the side.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: He doesn't leave documents lying around unless he's okay with other people reading them. It's fine, I promise.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cool, if you say so. Okay, let's see what he's got on Sachin...

talks.objective: Investigate the documents on the table

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was a lot of information... Paimon's getting a headache.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So to sum up, Sachin put the Akademiya in charge of managing his estate and went off to do research, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He even said that if he really liked one of the contestants, he wouldn't just give them a reward, but his entire estate as well... That must be worth heaps and heaps of Mora!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What!? Are you serious?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: All of Sachin's wealth, that's... more than I could spend in a lifetime, surely. Heck, if I got chosen, I'd be able to pay off all my debts, then buy a new place, and still have cash to burn...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I could build another Palace of Alcazarzaray... Except this time, I'd make it ten times bigger...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Then there's that new project in Port Ormos, of course — the bridge renovation. To do it properly would take upwards of—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, hey, snap out of it! You're getting way ahead of yourself there, mister!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You're right. First, I need to focus on winning and moving out of this place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait a moment, there's a loose slip of paper tucked in between these pages.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did Alhaitham write this? It looks like he was jotting ideas down as he was thinking things over. Hmm, let's see... Um, two phrases have been circled:

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Sachin, dead or alive? Unknown"... and "Diadem of Knowledge"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Some of this stuff is just plain incomprehensible. Is this written in some other language?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Let me see... Huh? I recognize this script. Hmm, give me a second...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: "Lofty ideals may provide no defense at all against nihilism, but perhaps little decisions can"... That's a rough translation, anyway. I can't guarantee it's one hundred percent accurate.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Hmm? There's another, smaller line of text underneath... Huh... Why would he bring that up?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it's so cool that you can actually read this script!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: We worked together on a project once when we were students — the title was "Decoding the Runes and Architectural Philosophy of the Ruins of King Deshret's Civilization." I had to familiarize myself a little with this script at the time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, interesting! So... Any idea what Alhaitham meant by all of this?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Heh. Who knows? The way his mind works is one of the great mysteries of the world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fair enough. Well, guess we've learned all we can here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's hope Aarav's made some progress.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, he'd better catch those crooks. But until then, uh... let's just head out for a stroll.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'm surprised anyone has the guts to try and pull off something like this during the Extravaganza. Just goes to show how tempting a fortune like Sachin's is.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: What would you do if a sum of Mora like that suddenly landed in your lap?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I don't know. I've never thought about it.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Come on, first thing off the top of your head. How would you spend it?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Hmm... Buying food, finding water sources... That kind of thing, I guess?

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Rest assured that I will bring these criminals to justice.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I fetched the documents for you. Feel free to look through them at your leisure.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I wonder where Alhaitham would go?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey... Isn't that the matra we investigated Siraj with?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Aarav," wasn't it? Let's go talk to him!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: (There's not much harm that a bunch of small-time crooks can do. But this whole Sachin affair... something about it strikes me as strange.)

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: (Mmm, this is good coffee.)

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: (Did he leave these notes there on purpose, or was this sheer coincidence? No... But if it wasn't a coincidence, then...)
